correctness.rationale: The exact positive Gram Schur complement h=w+A/4 and explicit block inverse reconstruct every signed evaluation kernel. Exact absolute-affine integrals give root and leaf norms. Monotonicity in each edge fraction, strict root/leaf separation, and convexity settle all norming locations and boundary cases. The phase identity has positive denominator. A genuine new-edge limit proves the discontinuity; 1,440 independent rational tests corroborate but do not replace the symbolic argument.

value.rationale: Sharp sup-norm stability of an L2 projector with arclength observations plus a positive atom at a junction is a motivated hybrid measurement problem. The exact all-degree formula yields nontrivial optimal evaluation locations, a phase transition at shortest-edge fractions one quarter and one third, and an explicit discontinuity when a new edge mass vanishes. These qualitative phenomena are not just a small numerical sharpening of the already-covered atom-free formula.
